first_remarks.remarks_to_the_author:
This manuscript presents a novel and compelling analysis of the role of ASB2a in the regulation of Th2 responses in vivo. A proteomic analysis revealed that ASB2a is required for filamin ubiquitylation and degradation, providing a mechanistic connection via integrin regulation. The effect is shown to be T cell autonomous through the use of in vitro and in vivo assays. Relevance is demonstrated in mouse models of asthma. The final figure introduces a pharmacological approach that seems promising, but in its current form actually detracts from the overall quality of the research.

Readers need to see more information about the screen, and all of the data. t-tests don't seem like an appropriate way to measure the effect of selected inhibitors in a screen of over 1000 molecules. What was the data structure in the screen, and how were hits selected?

Does TST change the ubiquitylation of FLNa or FLNb? Does it change the abundance of FLNb in Th2 cells? Does it change FLN abundance in an ASB2-dependent manner? Does it change cell shape or migration in an ASB-dependent manner? Or is it changing FLN expression in some independent way? The effects on cell migration and sphericity are far less robust with TST compared with ASB2 knockout.

The Th2 transfer model is useful since cells can be treated prior to transfer. Can TST be used in vivo (i.e. by systemic delivery or airway delivery)?

Figure 7a needs y-axis label. Figure 7b needs a scale for the heat map.

Overall, the inhibitor studies are incompletely documented, less developed, and less convincing than the rest of the manuscript. Removing them entirely would improve the manuscript and allow time to develop this work further for a more complete description elsewhere.

This manuscript explores whether the degradation of filamins (FLNa and FLNb) by ASB2α E3 ubiquitin ligase is a mechanism to sustain Th2 cell function, particularly their ability to migrate to inflamed tissues. The article concludes that low levels of FLNa and FLNb, because of high expression of ASB2α, allow efficient αvβ3 integrin-dependent cell migration of Th2 cells. Conversely, increased FLNa and FLNb levels due to ASB2α deficiency or altered function in Th2 cells reduce airway inflammation by diminishing Th2 recruitment to the lungs. Specifically, the data show that ASB2α is upregulated during Th2 polarization in vitro and controls FLNa/FLNb protein levels specifically in Th2 cells, with no impact on Th1, Th17, or Treg cells. RNAseq data from in vitro-generated Th2 cells show no gene expression differences between WT and ASB2α-deficient T cells, indicating ASB2α does not control Th2 differentiation in this context. The data also show that Th2 differentiation is accompanied by specific morphological changes and dynamic behavior that are not acquired in ASB2αdeficient T cells, suggesting that ASB2α-dependent degradation of FLNa and FLNb may be the cause of these morphological/motile changes. In mouse models of allergic inflammation, ASB2α-deficient mice show reduced allergic inflammation, mucus secretion, and remodeling, which correlates with decreased expression of Th2 cell cytokines and reduced frequency of Th2 cells in the lung and draining lymph nodes. To link the defect of ASB2α-deficient mice to a phenotype in T cells, the authors performed an experiment transferring in vitro Th2-polarized wild-type and ASB2α-deficient OTII cells into WT recipients and exposed them to ovalbumin (OVA). This experiment showed a reduced number of ASB2αdeficient donor T cells in the lung. Additionally, the authors identified thiostrepton (TST) as a drug targeting the ASB2αFLNa/b axis in T cells. They performed experiments with OVA-specific Th2 cells treated with TST before injection, showing reduced airway inflammation.

## Mayor points:

1. Although this study argues that efficient degradation of FLNa and FLNb and αvβ3 integrin function is important for T cell migration and recruitment to inflamed tissue but not for Th2 cell differentiation, the experimental setup in the present manuscript to demonstrate this is insufficient.
2. Previous studies have demonstrated that Integrin αvβ3 plays a crucial role in promoting optimal Th2 cell differentiation both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, αvβ3 expression is required to promote Thy1-αvβ3 interactions, which in turn enhance T-T interactions and Th2 cell differentiation by promoting FAK-mTOR signaling and IL-13/IL-5 production (PMID: 36550322). It is unclear how these previous results are reconciled with the data in this manuscript.
3. Thiostrepton (TST) is a natural antibiotic with pleiotropic properties. It has been shown to alter T cell proliferation, apoptosis and helper differentiation. Thus, it is not clear whether this drug specifically targets the ASB2α-FLNa/b axis without altering other functions in T cells.
4. The description of the experiments lacks sufficient detail to fully understand how the authors investigated the role of ASB2α, FLNa and FLNb, αvβ3 integrin in T cell migration and recruitment to inflamed tissue, as well as its impact on Th2 cell differentiation. More information about the experimental design, methods, and results would be needed to evaluate the validity and significance of the findings.

In this manuscript, Maire et al. have found that the mRNA levels of the E3 ubiquitin ligase ASB2α increased during the differentiation of naïve T cells to Th2 cells. ASB2α is involved in the proteolysis and degradation of filamins (FLN), a family of cytoskeletal proteins which are involved in cell motility and migration and are important for the regulation of the activation of integrins. The authors of this work have explored whether ASB2α may be involved in specific Th2 migration and functions. Using ASB2α KO mice, the authors found that, compared with control animals, the absence of ASB2α increased the levels of FLN in Th2 cells. FLN in ASB2α KO Th2 cells fostered the morphological phenotype of migrating cells and reduced the transcription of the integrin αvβ3 but not its protein expression, as determined by mass spectrometry. The authors also found that the inflammatory response to ovalbumin challenge was significantly less in ASB2α KO mice than in control animals, showing a significant reduction in the production of Th2-derived pro-inflammatory cytokines and the infiltration of inflammatory cells to lungs. Finally, the authors performed a small drug screening of compound capable of increasing the levels of FLN in HeLa cells. They were able to identify several drugs with functional activity on FLN preservation, but focused on the study of TST, which ameliorates Th2-mediated inflammation in a mouse model of allergy induced by the transference of OVA-specific OT2 Th2 lymphocytes.

## Major comment:

The manuscript by Maire et al. represents a further extension of the work by Gaylo-Moynihan et al., 2019 (Immunity 51: 298309), in which the characteristic mode of migration of Th2 lymphocytes and the role played by αvβ3 on it was formerly reported. On this occasion, focusing on experimental mouse models in which animals were challenged with ovalbumin or house dust mite (HDM) allergens, Maire et al. have explored the mechanism involved in αvβ3-mediated Th2 migration and its possible role in allergic inflammatory diseases with the aim of implementing interventional pharmacological approaches for the treatment of this group of diseases. The majority of the work would be considered well-performed and the results interesting, although some of them are of limited novelty (e.g. those corresponding to αvβ3 expression in T cell subsets).

## Specific points:

## 1.- Figure 1:

- a) The kinetics of the expression of ASB2α during Th2 cell differentiation should be studied at protein level (Western blot). f) In order to provide a better estimation of the expression levels of FLNa in control and ASB2α KO Th2 cells, the study of a housekeeping protein is required as control loading of the corresponding Western blot.
- h) Different FNLa expression levels between Th1 and Th2 cells are not convincing as shown. Densitometric analysis and quantification of at least three independent experiments is required.

## 2.- Figures 2 and 4:

The authors have studied how the deficiency of ASB2α affects Th2 morphology and motility. However, what about the overexpression of FLN? Does the transfection of FLN reduce Th2 motility? I wonder whether ASB2α degradation-resistant mutants of FLN would be generated in order to actually confirm the function of FLN proteolysis in ASB2-mediated cell migration.

- 3.- Figure 3: The authors clearly show that the protein expression levels of αvβ3 in control and in ASB2 KO Th2 cells are fairly similar. Then, what is the rationale of studying their expression at a transcriptional level and what do the differences found really mean? Would it not be better to study the activation status of this integrin by using specific antibodies? These sorts of Abs have been successfully used in previous studies (Pampori et al., 1999 J. Biol. Chem. 274: 21609-21616; Kioses et al., 2001 Nat Cell Biol 3: 316-320) and would be relevant in this case. In addition, ITGAV and ITGB3 Chip-seq results retrieved from a public database seem to not contribute enough to the more relevant manuscript's novel information and might not be presented among the main figures. It is worth noting that significant ITGAV and ITGB3 differences among T cell subsets were already reported by Gaylo-Moynihan et al. 2019. The same for figure panels 'd' and 'e' regarding ITGAV and ITGB3 relative expression in mouse T cells.
- 4.- Figure 4h-i: As presented, the results from these panels are not sufficiently novel since they show a well-known correlation between lymphocyte morphology and motility. In the absence of a comparative analysis of the relationship between cell morphology and motility in control and ASB2α KO Th2 cells, the contribution of this figure to the manuscript seems rather low.
- 5.- Fig 5c: On the corresponding dot plot analysis, what is the identity and significance of the high amounts of CD11c high, Siglec-F high, CD45+ cells depicted in the upper right corner of the dot graph corresponding to leukocyte infiltrates from ASB2α KO mouse lungs?
- 6.- The main functional results have been obtained from the studies performed in mice, but does ASB2α also regulate human Th2 cell functions? Does ASB2α promote migration of human T lymphocytes and the production of Th2-type proinflammatory cytokines through ubiquitination and degradation of FLN? The authors should study this issue in primary human Th2 lymphocytes generated in vitro.
- 7.- Figure 7: A legend to the Y axis on Figure 7a is required. The authors have characterized the inhibitory action of TST on FLNa degradation and how this compound regulates inflammation in an adoptive mouse model of allergy, but what about FLNb? Does TST regulate FLNb in a similarly extent as FLNa? What effect does FLNa exert in allergic inflammation? Figure 7b shows compounds with relative selectivity on the expression levels of FLNa and FNLb. Would these compounds be useful to study the possible contribution of each isoform of FLN to Th2-mediated inflammation?

unsorted.remarks_to_the_author: All of my prior concerns were addressed by removing the inhibitor studies from the manuscript.

In this revised manuscript, Maire et al. have satisfactorily addressed most of my major concerns. However, two points remain.

- 1.- New Fig. 6c should be clarified. What is represented on the flow cytometry dot plot? It seems to show cells in the lungs from OVA-stimulated mice. If so, it is difficult to understand why the corresponding quantification of CD45+, Siglec-F+, CD11c+ (typo on the y-axis legend of the right graph) alveolar macrophages is similar for OVA-treated ctrl and ASB2a KO animals. Qualitatively the dot plot seems to show that this subpopulation of cells is higher in ASB2a KO than in control animals. If the corresponding quantification is the result of several experiments, a more representative dot plot may be presented.
- 2.- Experiments with human T cells in new Figures 1k, l, and Sup. Figure 1g are interesting and improve the work. However, as broad protein synthesis considerably increases in T lymphocytes after activation and differentiation, results concerning ASB2a expression in Th2 cells would be more convincing if their levels were compared with Th1 instead of naïve T cells.

In the present work, Marie et al. investigated the role of ASB2α in degrading FLNa and b in Th2 lymphocytes and its role in Th2 cell differentiation, functions and migration. They clearly demonstrated that FLNa and FLNb are degraded by ASB2α whose expression is induced during Th2 differentiation and associated with FLNa and FLNb reduction (in both human and mice), compared to naïve or Th1 or Th17 cells. By using ASB2α ko mice, they also demonstrated that ASB2α-mediated degradation of FLNa and FLNb control morphological features and migration of Th2 cells, without affecting the transcriptomic signature of Th2 cells. The authors also show convincing data that ASB2α-mediated degradation of FLNa and FLNb is required for αvβ3 integrin activation and αvβ3 integrin-dependent migration in Th2 cells. Finally, by using mouse models of airway inflammation (OVA-induced) and asthma (HDM-induced) they demonstrated a crucial role of ASB2α in Th2 and eosinophil infiltration to the lungs and in inflammatory tissue dysfunctions (mucus secretion and collagen deposition).

The work is well performed and the results convincing and relevant for the future development of therapeutic drugs targeting ASB2α to dampen Th2-mediated inflammatory diseases.

## Minor points

The presentation of the results related to figure 6 and 7 need some revisions:

Lines 218-219: better explain cell infiltration (HE), mucus secretion (MT) and remodeling (collagen deposition) in Fig. 6a. Line 222: please specify that the number of CD4+ cells does not change in BAL, as clearly shown in Fig. 6g (left panel) Line 235: please correct and specify that the recruitment of CD4+ T cell to the lungs does not significantly change (p value = 0.08)

Lines 237-238: the results to Fig. 7g are not clear, the increase of FLNa in ko mice with HDM-induced asthma should be highlighted.

Figure 6c right panel: please correct Y axis label that should be CD45+ Siglec-F+ CD11c+ (macrophages), and not CD45+ Siglec-F+ CD11c- (eosinophils).

Since  these  two  issues  are  largely  interconnected,  our responses  to  both  of  them  are  grouped. To reinforce our data and elucidate the mechanisms by which increased levels of FLNa and FLNb in ASB2  -deficient Th2 lymphocytes inhibits  V  3  integrin-dependent cell migration, we have conducted new migration assays following activation or inhibition of integrins ( new Fig. 5 and new Supplementary Videos 3-10 ) .

These results are presented in the result section as follows (Page 5, lines 193-213):

'Accumulation of FLNa and FLNb inhibits  V  3 integrin-dependent migration of ASB2α-deficient Th2 lymphocytes by enhancing integrin activation

To  understand  how  FLNa  and  FLNb  accumulation  in  ASB2α-deficient  Th2  lymphocytes  inhibits  cell migration, we challenged the two models linking FLNa to inhibition of integrin-dependent cell motility. In the first model, FLNa maintains integrins in an inactive state 21 . In a second model, FLNa promotes integrin outside-in signaling leading to inhibition of dynamic cell movement 24 . We first studied by live imaging the dynamics of ctrl and ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes treated with MnCl2 to activate integrins and allowed to migrate onto vitronectin-coated slides (Supplementary Videos). Compared to untreated ctrl Th2 lymphocytes, MnCl2-treated ctrl Th2 lymphocytes exhibited a diminished track displacement

length and a reduced cell velocity that were similar to those measured in untreated or in MnCl2-treated ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes (Supplementary Videos 3-6 and Fig. 5a-d), suggesting that integrins are more activated in ASB2α-deficient Th2 lymphocytes than in ctrl T2 lymphocytes. We then assessed the dynamics of ctrl and ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes treated with a combination of anti- V  and anti- 3 integrin blocking antibodies to inhibit integrins. As expected, following  V  3 integrin inhibition, ctrl Th2 lymphocytes showed decrease track displacement length and decreased cell velocity compared  to untreated cells  in  agreement  with  the  role  of  the  V  3  integrin  in  Th2  lymphocyte  migration  cells (Supplementary Videos 7-8 and Fig. 5e-h). In contrast, following  V  3 integrin inhibition, ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes exhibited an enhanced track displacement length and an increased cell velocity compared to untreated cells (Supplementary Videos 9-10 and Fig. 5e-h), reinforcing the view that increased levels of  FLNa  and  FLNb  in ASB2 cKO  Th2  lymphocytes  leads  to  abnormal  V  3  integrin-dependent  cell migration.'

And discussed as follows (Page 8, lines 324-328): 'Our data also provide evidences that accumulation of FLNa and FLNb in ASB2α-deficient in Th2 lymphocyte inhibits  V  3 integrin-dependent cell migration by enhancing αV 3 integrin outside-in signaling. In line with these findings, it is tempting to speculate that fine-tuning levels of FLNa and FLNb is critical to optimal  V  3 integrin-dependent cell migration of Th2 lymphocytes.'

The effects of ASB2  loss and FLNa/FLNb accumulation on Th2 lymphocyte differentiation and identity was addressed on a global scale by RNA-seq. As shown in Fig. 1n and Supplementary Fig. 2a-d, Th2specific  genes  exhibited  similar  expression  patterns  in  ctrl  and ASB2 cKO  Th2  lymphocytes, demonstrating no impact of ASB2 deletion on the transcriptomic program of Th2 lymphocytes.

Taken together, our results indicate a coordinated regulation of ASB2  and  V  3 integrin expression in Th2 lymphocytes and point to a role of low levels of FLNa and FLNb for efficient migration of Th2 lymphocytes to build an efficient Th2 lymphocyte response as the mechanism downstream of ASB2  .

2. Previous studies have demonstrated that Integrin αvβ3 plays a crucial role in promoting optimal Th2 cell differentiation both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, αvβ3 expression is required to promote Thy1-αvβ3 interactions, which in turn enhance T-T interactions and Th2 cell differentiation by promoting FAK-mTOR signaling and IL-13/IL-5 production (PMID: 36550322). It is unclear how these previous results are reconciled with the data in this manuscript.

The  reviewer  makes  an  important  point.  As  mentioned  above,  Th2-specific  genes  including  those encoding type 2 cytokines exhibited similar expression patterns in ctrl and ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes generated ex vivo , indicating that ASB2α does not play a role in regulating the expression of Th2 genes and the production of IL-13 and IL-5. Collectively, these data strongly suggested that the mechanisms linking Thy1-αvβ3 integrin interactions to enhanced Th2 lymphocyte differentiation and increased IL13/IL-5  production  (Szeto  et  al.,  Nature  Immunology  24,  123-135,  2022)  is  unlikely  to  rely  on  the abundance of FLNa and FLNb. As requested, we have now discussed our data in lines of this previous study in the discussion section as follows (Page 7, lines 282-285): 'Because Th2-specific genes including those encoding type 2 cytokines exhibited similar expression patterns in ctrl and ASB2α-deficient Th2 lymphocytes, the mechanisms linking Thy1-αvβ3 integrin interactions to enhanced Th2 lymphocyte differentiation and increased IL-13/IL-5 production 39 is unlikely to rely on the abundance of FLNa and FLNb.'

3. Thiostrepton (TST) is a natural antibiotic with pleiotropic properties. It has been shown to alter T cell proliferation, apoptosis and helper differentiation. Thus, it is not clear whether this drug specifically targets the ASB2α-FLNa/b axis without altering other functions in T cells.

As proposed by the Editor and Reviewer 1, the inhibitor studies have been removed from the revised manuscript to develop this work further for a more complete description elsewhere.

The reviewer suggested over-expressing FLNa or FLNb in Th2 lymphocytes to investigate the effects of overexpression of filamins  on  Th2  morphology  and motility.  However,  we  already  know  that  overexpressed FLNa and FLNb are very efficiently degraded in ASB2  -expressing cells indicating that this is not an efficient approach to reverse the effects of ASB2  -mediated degradation of FLNa and FLNb. We therefore believe that such FLNa mutant would not be a good tool to confirm the function of FLNa/b proteolysis in ASB2  -mediated cell migration. ## 'Accumulation of FLNa and FLNb inhibits  V  3 integrin-dependent migration of ASB2α-deficient Th2 lymphocytes by enhancing integrin activation

To  understand  how  FLNa  and  FLNb  accumulation  in  ASB2α-deficient  Th2  lymphocytes  inhibits  cell migration, we challenged the two models linking FLNa to inhibition of integrin-dependent cell motility. In the first model, FLNa maintains integrins in an inactive state 21 . In a second model, FLNa promotes integrin outside-in signaling leading to inhibition of dynamic cell movement 24 . We first studied by live imaging the dynamics of ctrl and ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes treated with MnCl2 to activate integrins and allowed to migrate onto vitronectin-coated slides (Supplementary Videos). Compared to untreated ctrl Th2 lymphocytes, MnCl2-treated ctrl Th2 lymphocytes exhibited a diminished track displacement length and a reduced cell velocity that were similar to those measured in untreated or in MnCl2-treated ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes (Supplementary Videos 3-6 and Fig. 5a-d), suggesting that integrins are more activated in ASB2α-deficient Th2 lymphocytes than in ctrl T2 lymphocytes. We then assessed the dynamics of ctrl and ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes treated with a combination of anti- V  and anti- 3 integrin blocking antibodies to inhibit integrins. As expected, following  V  3 integrin inhibition, ctrl Th2 lymphocytes showed decrease track displacement length and decreased cell velocity compared  to untreated cells  in  agreement  with  the  role  of  the  V  3  integrin  in  Th2  lymphocyte  migration  cells (Supplementary Videos 7-8 and Fig. 5e-h). In contrast, following  V  3 integrin inhibition, ASB2 cKO Th2 lymphocytes exhibited an enhanced track displacement length and an increased cell velocity compared to untreated cells (Supplementary Videos 9-10 and Fig. 5e-h), reinforcing the view that increased levels of  FLNa  and  FLNb  in ASB2 cKO  Th2  lymphocytes  leads  to  abnormal  V  3  integrin-dependent  cell migration.'
